tools.name: manage_belief

tools.description: Manage per-entity evidence, reconciled belief stances, and the append-only perception ledger — one entity's subjective epistemic state, distinct from objective truth and shared lore. admit takes a subject/predicate/object proposition with a 0..1 weight and derives its question; source defaults to the active badge; retract suppresses evidence without deleting the ledger; reconcile recomputes stances after evidence changes. The perception ledger is append-only and not reversible via manage_history, so correct a mistaken admit with retract. Use when: recording or inspecting what an entity learned or believes, finding contradictions, or logging perceptions. Do NOT use when: recording objective world truth — use manage_causality (action: causal_propose); recording shared lore — use manage_lore.

tools.name: manage_session
tools.title: Session Management
tools.description: Manage play-facing session controls: recap, verbosity, briefing_order, and tool discovery, distinct from story content and Novel lifecycle. recap summarizes recent activity and accepts session_id, gm_notes, and a history window; discover searches the tool catalog by name, description, or title. verbosity sets normal or terse output; briefing_order reorders briefing sections and requires the GM or Editor badge. verbosity is session-scoped; briefing_order persists to the Novel. recap and discover are read-only, and a setting is restored by setting it again (no undo snapshot is taken). Use when: recapping play, tuning output verbosity, reordering the briefing, or finding a tool. Do NOT use when: health, audit compaction, event-log, or category operations — use manage_diagnostics; recording story content — use manage_story (action: record).

params.category: New category label, or null/empty to restore the default (category).
params.gm_notes: GM-only free-text notes returned only to the Game Master badge (recap).
params.max_entries: Positive integer; returns a non-mutating summarize prompt over the most recent entries (compress).
params.query: Optional search term matched against tool name, description, and title (discover).
params.session_id: Archived session id to include in recap (recap).
params.sessions: Number of recent sessions to retain live; triggers irreversible compaction (compact; default TTRPG_AUDIT_RETENTION_SESSIONS).
params.supersede: Ordinal of an event this observation replaces (event).
params.through_ordinal: Return events up to and including this ordinal (history).

output_fields.status: Machine-readable result status: OK, NEED_INPUT, WARNING, PARTIAL, or an error category (REQ-002, REQ-548c).
output_fields.text: Human-readable text envelope mirroring the structured result (REQ-001, REQ-548a).

tools.name: manage_staging
tools.title: Scene Staging Management
tools.description: Manage scene presence and autonomy staging. Use when: setting which entities are present (presence) or adjusting NPC and world autonomy for the scene (autonomy). Do NOT use when: setting the scene, issuing a directive, offering choices, or consulting the oracle — use manage_scene. presence and autonomy persist to the Novel and are audited; revert with manage_history (action: undo).

params.adventure_scene: Adventure-scene waypoint anchor; empty or null clears (set).
params.beat: Story-beat tag (set): setup, escalation, turning_point, climax, resolution, denouement.
params.question: Question to resolve (oracle).

tools.name: manage_story
tools.title: Story Journal Management
tools.description: Manage the story journal — typed narrative memories (decision, moment, revelation, bond, consequence). record appends an entry and consumes the turn_handle minted by take_turn; update edits a mutable entry; decision and consequence entries are immutable and refuse update or promotion; remove deletes an entry by index; promote copies an entry into lore under a derived or supplied key. list filters by type and paginates with offset and limit, returning previews unless detail is set. Mutations require the GM or Editor badge, persist to the Novel, and are undoable via manage_history (action: undo); list is read-only. Use when: recording, editing, removing, listing, or promoting story beats. Do NOT use when: recording a durable world fact — use manage_lore (action: set).

params.turn_handle: Turn handle minted by take_turn (record); consumed on success.

output_fields.status: Machine-readable result status: OK, NEED_INPUT, WARNING, PARTIAL, or an error category (REQ-002, REQ-548c).
output_fields.text: Human-readable text envelope mirroring the structured result (REQ-001, REQ-548a).

tools.name: manage_synthesis
tools.title: Synthesis Management
tools.description: Manage synthesis content (voice examples, lore templates, action patterns, and other Ruleset Wisdom). Mutating actions persist to the Novel and are audited; read-only actions do not mutate state. Revert the most recent mutation with manage_history (action: undo). activate/deactivate with key omitted act on the whole module. Use when: running, reverting, listing, activating, deactivating, toggling, or player-authoring synthesis items. Do NOT use when: browsing the codex — use manage_codex (action: list).

tools.name: manage_vow
tools.title: Vow Management
tools.description: Track narrative vows, quests, and obligations with milestones. set creates a vow and links a countdown whose ticks follow the difficulty rank track (scope defaults to shared); milestone advances progress; resolve and forsake close the vow with distinct outcomes (fulfilled vs abandoned). Mutations require the GM or Editor badge and persist to the Novel; list is read-only. Vow changes are not reversible via manage_history; resolve and forsake are terminal choices. Use when: setting, advancing, resolving, forsaking, or listing vows. Do NOT use when: starting a clock timer — use manage_countdown (action: set).

params.difficulty: troublesome, dangerous, formidable, extreme, or epic (set).
params.name: Vow name (set).

output_fields.status: Machine-readable result status: OK, NEED_INPUT, WARNING, PARTIAL, or an error category (REQ-002, REQ-548c).
output_fields.text: Human-readable text envelope mirroring the structured result (REQ-001, REQ-548a).

tools.name: manage_world
tools.title: World Model Management
tools.description: Manage the world model — rooms, things, exits, and their spatial properties. create, update, remove, convert, and generate mutate the model and persist to the Novel; removing a room or thing is permanent — re-create it to restore the model. create_exit links both directions; create_thing honors location_type only when location is set, and kind forces property defaults. There are no read-only actions here; inspect state with run_command (action: execute). Use when: creating, updating, removing, bulk-converting, or generating locations and objects. Do NOT use when: navigating the world — use run_command (action: execute) or run_command (action: resolve); proposing or admitting objective-state transitions — use manage_causality; recording what an entity believes — use manage_belief.

params.causal_entity: Entity whose objective state is proposed (causal_propose).
params.causal_scope: Scope coordinate (causal_propose; default the active Novel slug).
params.causal_source_ordinal: Contributing event-log ordinal (causal_propose; default the latest event).
params.climbable: When true the thing can be climbed (create_thing/update_thing).
params.drinkable: When true the thing can be drunk (create_thing/update_thing).
params.edible: When true the thing can be eaten (create_thing/update_thing).
params.enterable: When true the thing can be entered (create_thing/update_thing).
params.fixed: When true the thing cannot be taken (create_thing/update_thing).
params.key: Bound key thing name required to unlock or lock this thing when lockable (create_thing/update_thing).
params.lit: When true the thing is lit (create_thing/update_thing).
params.lockable: When true the thing can be locked (create_thing/update_thing).
params.locked: When true the thing starts locked (create_thing/update_thing).
params.name: Room/thing name (create/update/remove).
params.openable: When true the thing can be opened (create_thing/update_thing).
params.read_text: Text revealed when the thing is read (create_thing/update_thing).
params.readable: When true the thing can be read (create_thing/update_thing).
params.switchable: When true the thing can be switched (create_thing/update_thing).
params.switched_on: When true the thing is switched on (create_thing/update_thing).
params.transparent: When true the thing is transparent (create_thing/update_thing).
params.wearable: When true the thing can be worn (create_thing/update_thing).

tools.name: open_session
tools.title: Open Play Session
tools.description: Open a play session by resuming a Novel, activating a badge, and returning a recap. Use when: starting or resuming a session (open_session), especially after a restart. Do NOT use when: creating a Novel — use manage_novel (action: create); running a turn — use take_turn. Resume and badge changes persist and are audited; revert with manage_history (action: undo).

tools.name: resolve_mechanic
tools.title: Resolve Mechanics
tools.description: Resolve uncertain actions across the host's base mechanics: Fate Fudge dice, aspects, Fate points, and stress; Ironsworn momentum, moves, and progress; Forged action rolls, stress, trauma, and downtime; and generic ruleset table rolls. Rolls and state changes persist to the Novel and are audited; a roll with no following write is flagged as an uncommitted roll. Revert the most recent mutation with manage_history (action: undo). fate_roll uses dF, ironsworn_move compares an action die against two challenge dice, and forged_action_roll takes the highest of a d6 pool. Use when: resolving a Fate, Ironsworn, or Forged mechanic, or rolling on a ruleset generation table. Do NOT use when: resolving a ruleset skill check — use the bound ruleset's roll tools; managing vows — use manage_vow (action: set).

params.adds: Stat and bonuses added to the action die (ironsworn_move).
params.amount: Fate points (fate_point), stress (fate_stress, forged_stress, forged_downtime), or momentum (ironsworn_momentum); defaults to 1.
params.burn: Burn momentum to replace the action score (ironsworn_move).
params.cost: Stress cost to resist (forged_stress); defaults to 2.
params.dice: Fudge dice notation (fate_roll) or dice pool size (forged_action_roll).
params.entity_id: Entity or NPC id (fate_aspect, fate_point, fate_stress, ironsworn_momentum, ironsworn_move, forged_stress, forged_downtime).
params.modifier: Skill rating added to the roll (fate_roll).
params.name: Aspect name, progress-track name, move name, action name, or consequence label.
params.op: Sub-operation for aspect, fate_point, stress, momentum, progress, or downtime.
params.seed: Deterministic seed (fate_roll, ironsworn_move, ironsworn_progress, forged_action_roll, roll).
params.shifts: Shifts to mark on a stress track (fate_stress); defaults to 1.
params.skill: Skill name for the roll label (fate_roll).
params.slug: Ruleset slug for a Novel-independent roll (roll).
params.target: Aspect target: 'scene' or an entity/NPC id (fate_aspect); defaults to 'scene'.
params.track: Stress track to mark or clear (fate_stress).

tools.name: respond_decision
tools.title: Respond to Workflow Decision
tools.description: Answer a pending workflow decision, atomically draining it and persisting the outcome to the Novel. option must match one of the emitted choices; 'cancel' aborts the workflow and restores its pre-workflow snapshot, while any applied outcome is not reversible. The drain is mutating and audited, and a second call with no pending decision returns STATE_CONFLICT. Use when: the server emitted a [NEED_INPUT] prompt and the caller must choose. Do NOT use when: no decision is pending — use set_badge or a state tool instead.

params.decision: The canonical decision text the workflow is waiting on.
params.option: The chosen option, or 'cancel' to abort the workflow and restore its snapshot.

output_fields.status: Machine-readable result status: OK, NEED_INPUT, WARNING, PARTIAL, or an error category (REQ-002, REQ-548c).
output_fields.text: Human-readable text envelope mirroring the structured result (REQ-001, REQ-548a).

tools.name: run_command
tools.title: Parser Command
tools.description: Execute a parser command, resolve a spatial intent, or map intent to tool calls. execute runs a parsed verb-and-noun command (for example 'take lamp' or 'go north') against the world model, mutates world/entity state, persists to the Novel, and is audited; a mistaken move is reversed by issuing the inverse command because no undo snapshot is taken. resolve computes a movement outcome without mutating, and suggest returns recommended tool calls for an intent. On a ruleset-bound Novel the parser is GM-only for navigation and mutation, while the Player badge keeps read-only perception commands. Use when: a player or narrator takes a physical action (execute), needs a movement outcome without mutating state (resolve), or wants intent mapped to tools (suggest). Do NOT use when: the GM inspects the model directly — use manage_world or manage_lore.

params.intent: The intent to resolve or map (resolve/suggest).

output_fields.status: Machine-readable result status: OK, NEED_INPUT, WARNING, PARTIAL, or an error category (REQ-002, REQ-548c).
output_fields.text: Human-readable text envelope mirroring the structured result (REQ-001, REQ-548a).

tools.name: set_badge
tools.title: Set Active Badge
tools.description: Switch the active badge to player, game_master, observer, or none (Editor), gating tool access server-side for the active Novel; always callable. Switching immediately re-filters tools/list, so a narrower badge can revoke tools mid-task and switching back restores them; badge changes are mutating session state, audited, and reversible by switching back. Use when: entering the story, spectating, or stepping away to edit. Do NOT use when: answering a pending workflow decision — use respond_decision.

params.badge: The badge to activate: player, game_master, observer, or none (Editor).

tools.name: take_turn
tools.title: Take Play Turn
tools.description: Resolve a player intent through the parser and mint a turn handle for the story record. Use when: taking a turn (take_turn) before recording the outcome with manage_story (action: record). Do NOT use when: resolving a specific combat round — use manage_combat (action: advance); rolling a ruleset check — use resolve_mechanic (action: roll). The turn is read-only and non-persistent: no Novel state is mutated; the handle is session-scoped and expires.
